Methods

Molecular dynamics simulations were performed on the apo and ligand-bound
forms of the kinase using OpenMM 8.1 with the AMBER ff14SB force field for
the protein. Ligand parameters were derived from the General Amber Force
Field (GAFF2) with AM1-BCC partial charges, generated using AmberTools
24. Each system was solvated in a cubic TIP3P water box with a minimum
distance of 10 Å between the protein and any box edge, and neutralised by
adding NaCl to a physiological concentration of 150 mM. The final solvated
systems contained approximately 42,000 atoms.

Energy minimisation was performed using a maximum of 5,000 steps of
steepest descent until the maximum force fell below 10 kJ mol⁻¹ nm⁻¹.
The system was then equilibrated for 100 ps in the NVT ensemble at 300 K
using a Langevin thermostat with a friction coefficient of 1 ps⁻¹.
Heavy-atom positional restraints with a force constant of 1000 kJ mol⁻¹
nm⁻² were applied during NVT equilibration to prevent excessive rearrangement
near the binding pocket. A second equilibration of 500 ps in the NPT
ensemble at 1 bar was performed using a Monte Carlo barostat to release
the restraints and equilibrate the system density.

Production simulations were run for 100 ns in the NPT ensemble with a
2 fs time step. Bonds involving hydrogen atoms were constrained using
the SHAKE algorithm to permit the longer time step. Particle Mesh Ewald
(PME) was used for long-range electrostatics with a 1.0 nm real-space
cutoff and a Fourier spacing of 0.12 nm.

Trajectories were saved every 10 ps for analysis and energies / temperature
were logged every 1 ps. RMSD of the protein Cα atoms relative to the
initial frame was computed using MDTraj 1.10. RMSF per residue was
calculated after superposing each frame to the average structure of the
last 50 ns. Three independent replicas were performed for each system to
assess sampling adequacy; this fixture describes a single replica.

Analysis: structural drift was assessed via Cα RMSD; ligand pose stability
was tracked via heavy-atom RMSD restricted to the ligand atom selection.
The radius of gyration was monitored to detect any unfolding events.
